verdict.rationale: Oneleet's first-party docs describe an official Oneleet MCP server. You add it to your assistant and connect through an OAuth browser login with workspace selection, or use scoped service keys for agent automation. The assistant acts with the member's role permissions, and every action is attributed to that member. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP server working, documentation of the specific MCP tools/capabilities exposed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: add the Oneleet MCP server to your assistant, and it opens a browser window where you log in to Oneleet, review what the assistant is asking for, and pick the workspace it should work in.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows, every action is attributed to your account
Use **service keys** for AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace.
Any member can connect — no admin involvement is required — but what the assistant can do is limited by that member’s role.
